result:
The proposed answer is incorrect, as a check at s = 1 shows.

For s = 1, the HRS code is the ordinary Reed–Solomon code of dimension t on r points. Its Schur square is the Reed–Solomon code of polynomials of degree at most 2t−2, so it has dimension min(r, 2t−1).

The hypothesis t ≤ (r+2s−1)/2 becomes t ≤ (r+1)/2 when s = 1, which means 2t−1 ≤ r. So the square has dimension 2t−1.

The proposed formula gives min(r, t(t+1)/2). Take t = 3 and r ≥ 5, which satisfies p ≥ t ≥ 2s when p ≥ 3. The formula gives 6, but the true dimension is 5.

The solution asserts that the square reaches the symmetric-square bound binom(t+1, 2) without proof, and this is false even in the simplest case.

VERDICT: REJECT
